To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) all single field models of inflation can be described in a common language, the effective field theory, (ii) the most relevant high energy corrections are those that reduce the speed of sound, (iii) these corrections are constrained by experiments and (iv) they are correlated with the level of non-Gaussianty.

(i) the effective field theory (EFT) of inflation is a powerful tool to describe the dynamics of inflationary models, (ii) the EFT of inflation is a generalization of the EFT of dark energy, and (iii) the EFT is the natural language to describe single field inflationary models, including those that violate the standard assumptions of slow-roll and adiabaticity.

the EFT of inflation is the most general single-field theory of a light scalar field on a quasi-de Sitter background, and that the EFT approach allows one to derive the general relations between different observables in a single field model, including the speed of sound and the non-Gaussianity, as well as the relation between the non-linearly realized time reparametrizations and the reduced speed of sound.
